key_insight: Autoregressive quantum circuit synthesis works well when approximate outputs can be corrected afterward, but it breaks down for exact discrete circuits as early token errors cascade into large decoding drift.
engineering_relevance: For fault-tolerant quantum compilation, inference-time search and more training data can improve exact synthesis, but reliability still degrades on longer target circuits where exact equivalence is mandatory.
method: 44.8M-parameter encoder-decoder transformer with structured circuit tokenization
Tested on parameterized circuits (2-6 qubits) and Clifford+T circuits (3-6 qubits)
Used equivalence verification, multi-candidate decoding, and scaling experiments to measure drift mitigation
evidence_signal: On Clifford+T circuits, exact-match accuracy fell from 88% for circuits with <=9 gates to near zero beyond 26 gates, while multi-candidate selection improved exact-match from 7% to 22.5% and 2.5x more training data raised it to 39.5%.
watch_item: The approach remains fragile for long exact-synthesis targets, since even with more data the accuracy still drops sharply with circuit length and cannot be recovered by post-processing.
paper_title: When Close Enough Is Not Enough: Autoregressive Drift in Quantum Circuit Synthesis
